meta_description:
lakshmisharath on September 3, 2026: "This is Lord Krishna’s office. Across the sea is his home,” my driver said as we entered Dwarka.

The salt of the sea filled the air. Somewhere beneath lies Krishna’s submerged city, believed lost to the sea.

Photos 1–3 | Krishna’s kingdom by the sea

To the people here, Dwarka is not just a temple town. Krishna is worshipped as a king and Dwarkadhish Temple as his palace—Jagat Mandir. Bells chimed, drums rose and red flags fluttered above its towers.

Photos 4–6 | Across the sea to Krishna’s home

The next morning, I followed Krishna across the sea. Colourful boats filled Okha harbour, seagulls circled above us and pilgrims sailed to Bet Dwarka, believed to be his island home. A room inside the temple remembers Krishna’s reunion with Sudama; devotees still receive rice, recalling Sudama’s humble gift.

Photo 7 | The queen who stands apart

Back on the mainland stood Rukmini Temple, separated from Krishna’s temple by the legend of Durvasa’s curse.

Photos 8–9 | A friendship remembered

In Porbandar, Sudama’s home, murals inside Sudama Temple brought their enduring friendship to life.

Photos 10–15 | Krishna’s final journey

Near Somnath, the Krishna trail became quieter. Banganga, Bhalka Tirth and Dehotsarg are associated with his final journey—where a hunter’s arrow is believed to have struck him and where he is said to have left his mortal form.

Beside his footprints at Dehotsarg, I realised that my trail had ended. I had followed Krishna’s footsteps through this mythical land.

Photos 16–17 | Back where the journey began

The sea fell quiet at sunset; the red flag flew above Krishna’s kingdom.

SAVE THIS 4-DAY DWARKA–SOMNATH ITINERARY

Day 1: Dwarkadhish Temple and sunset; stay in Dwarka.
Day 2: Rukmini Temple and Bet Dwarka via Sudarshan Setu; stay in Dwarka.
Day 3: Porbandar (104 km) for Sudama Temple; continue to Somnath (130 km). Stay in Somnath/Veraval.
Day 4: Somnath, Banganga, Bhalka Tirth and Dehotsarg.

TIPS: A cab/self-drive car is easiest. Dwarka has a railway station; airports: Jamnagar and Porbandar. Visit October–February. Janmashtami is crowded. Photography is restricted 

#KrishnaJayanthi #Dwarka #BetDwarka #somnath".
